report:
Initial stage, as preserved in the supplied prior findings: direct SS hydration came from A04 and A08 (2 accounts), joint Avant Guard–SS retention from A09 (1), direct SS texture from A03 and A04 (2), and speculative SS texture from none. Hydration was independently repeated by two credited retailer origins under different routines. Lightweight/fast-drying and comparatively sticky reports did not establish a uniform texture. A07's exact record remained 'undefined...' after retrieval; its experience was unavailable.

Updated stage: A13 adds a third credited retailer origin directly reporting SS hydration, including plump, hydrated skin after a 12-hour shift. The shared proposition—reported SS hydration within users' routines—is independently repeated across A04, A08 and A13, without cross-venue corroboration. A04 uses it before makeup; A08 pairs it with tretinoin and other actives; A13 describes oily T-zone, dry sensitive cheeks and mild rosacea. A13 alone adds reduced irritation/reactivity, no forehead congestion and perceived lower oil production; those specific outcomes are not all independently repeated. A09 remains joint mask–SS retention evidence with no separable allocation. No direct SS hydration opposition appears in readable focal testimony, but A07 remains substantively unavailable. Objective efficacy, prevalence and isolated causation are unestablished.

Direct SS texture now has three focal accounts. A13 describes sticky, shiny, slick wear, generally favors nighttime use and sometimes wears a pump outside despite shine; smaller amounts are presented as more wearable. This adds another account describing SS stickiness alongside A03's first-hand comparison with less-sticky Wave Serum. However, A03's independence is unavailable, so two source accounts do not warrant two credited independent origins. A04's lightweight, refreshing, fast-drying experience remains supported. These observations create a mixed/conditional feel profile, not proof that one report is false; dose and routine may matter but have not been demonstrated to explain the differences. A13's claims about what most people will tolerate and what stickiness accomplishes exceed its own experience. A17 adds one explicitly non-user speculation that SS is thicker than Wave, based on stated glycerin percentages; it cannot corroborate experienced SS thickness or hydration.

Behavior consequences remain bounded: A04 narrates ordering SS after a sister's introduction, buying Buffer Jelly for greater nighttime hydration/repair, and subsequently buying face wash and mesh moisturizer. Hydration is not established as the reason for every acquisition; refill metadata adds no narrated repurchase. A03 continues SS despite stickiness because of its believed higher glycerin content. A13 accepts shine on some outings; its advice to avoid sticky products is not personal abandonment. A09's mask-fit complaint produces a star deduction alongside retention praise. A14 reports free Buffer Jelly receipt and calls itself a convert after two uses, not a completed paid purchase or repurchase. A15 considered returning Plasma Wash because of severe eye burning; no completed return or remedy is reported. No focal completed repurchase is narrated.

Other-product evidence stays separate. A10's overnight retention and glow concern Buffer Jelly with unspecified hydrating products. A14 describes Buffer Jelly's jelly-to-oil, silky feel and soft, calm skin when mixed into nighttime moisturizer; it supplies no SS texture or hydration testimony. Its explicit free-product disclosure remains material despite metadata marked rewarded=false. A15 praises Plasma Wash's silky texture but reports poor cleansing, severe eye burning and greater dryness, including after two washes. This contrasts with A04's favorable face-wash account at the cleanser level, not with SS hydration; defect versus technique remains A15's unresolved question. A18 praises Wave hydration and reports C.R.E.A.M nighttime moisture-retention failure and sunscreen pilling. A17's detailed C.R.E.A.M discussion includes mixing with Wave for easier use and wanting another, oily layer; that offers related other-product experience, not exact repetition of every A18 outcome. Its explicit agreement does not donate SS testimony. Both share one Reddit thread and have unavailable independence postures.

Material context: the A18 parent record is the same orchidmommy account and statement as focal A18, not another source. Context-only Skin_Fanatic asks about a better moisturizer while saying it has not tried C.R.E.A.M (score 2); this is interest, not use. Previously supplied context-only hillary_____k reports buying Level Serum on Black Friday, brighter/even skin and emphatic future repurchase intention (score 24), not SS experience or completed repurchase. The common Regimen Lab discovery post provides topic context; its actor and engagement are unavailable. Product pages and metadata resolve product references and skin/variant scope without adding testimony.

Raw engagement: all eight focal Junip accounts have 0 up-votes/0 down-votes. Reddit scores are A03=6, A17=7 and A18=10, each explicitly material_positive=false/not_interpreted. Engagement observation times are unavailable, including context scores. No material resonance posture is established; likes/scores do not verify experiences, independence, prevalence or buying effects. Formulas/versions are unknown throughout; unspecified SS variants remain unknown. Counts below are updated focal source-account counts, not origin or event counts. Review-update timestamps and repeated context do not establish additional experiences. Earlier findings were carried forward from the supplied prior record without fresh retrieval.
